title: Hey there, can anyone help a long-time noob?

posts.author: RPG_Girl
posts.body:
Alright, back in 2020 I did a free trial on RPG MV and liked it. So I made an account and started saving up money to get MV so I could try and make a game for real. But due to how school was back then I couldn't really get to actually bring that want into something real. Right now, I want to at least try to make a demo for a game idea I have, which is making sort of horror comedy game. Unfortunately, I have retained no knowledge from 2020 me so i'm stuck all the way back at square one. Anybody got any recommendations for tutorials or tile sets to start off with?
I appreciate any help you guys could give!
-RPG_Girl

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome! Glad you are able to move forward with your interest now.
Recreating tutorials is a great place to start. When I was first learning, I just searched for RPG Maker MZ (MV for you) Tutorials and I found too many to count. I selected several series by creators that covered most of the basics and advanced concepts.
And the great thing is the many MV tutorials can be applicable to MZ and many MZ tutorials can be applicable to MV. But it is important to do a bit of research on how the two versions are different. So if you watch a tutorial for MZ to learn a concept, you can better tell if it should work in MV.
Once you get a good grasp on things by recreating tutorials, just experimenting and trying things in an experiments project can really help too.
This forum can be very helpful on your journey.
Good luck on your projects and remember to enjoy what you do!

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
In the passed I've been teaching new users how to use RPG maker a lot. I even made a discord server, just to help noobs. Believe me, those noobs kept me busy.
Yet I never, ever advised watching tutorials for the basics.
Instead, I tell my uhm... my students? my pupils? my noobs? Well, I tell the noobs to take a new project, and try out each and every function in the event editor. Some will be obvious in what they do, and others are less obvious. The once that are less obvious, are explained in the engine, when you hover over the function with your mouse. If that isn't helpful either, or the user is still confused, they would ask me.
I will give you the same advice as I give all the boobs that come to me for help:
First, experiment with the next 3 functions:
Control Switch
Control Variable
Conditional Branch
No matter what you make with RPG maker, you really can't do without those. Pretty much everything you will make, will need to use switches, variables and/or conditions.
The reason I don't like to recommend tutorials on the basics is: When something gets explained to you, you might remember it for an hour or a day. You might think you understand, until you actually try to put it in practice, then it turns out it wasn't as clear as it seemed. But when you figure things out by trying and thinking yourself what the solution would be, you won't forget that in a long time.
I'm not saying tutorials can't be great, but I wouldn't use it for the basics. If you have something specific you want to do, like making a lockpick mechanism on a door, or resurrect enemies after 60 seconds, you might want to start using tutorials. But when you just want to learn the basics, there is really no better way then to just try out every button and see what happens.
last comment: Don't be scared to break anything. If you make a project purely to experiment in, and it happens to break, then that is fine too. That is why you experiment in a dummy project, and not in your main project. If it breaks, you can just start a new project and try again. But then again, it is kind of hard to break a projects using basic controls.
Anyhow, good luck. I hope you find this useful.
